exercise.name: Dumbbell Russian Twist with Legs off the Floor
aliases: Dumbbell seated twist, feet off the floor

reference.title: Dumbbell Russian Twist with Legs Floor Off
reference.listing: Page not read (gymvisual.com is blocked by the proxy); movement taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice.
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you turn to each side, breathe in through the middle.
breathing.cadence: About 1.3 s per side with a short pause

prescription.tempo: About 1 s turn, short pause each side
prescription.load: User-chosen dumbbell; light to moderate, held by the ends
prescription.progression: Bodyweight Russian twist first; then feet up, then a heavier dumbbell

cues.text: Sit with knees bent, lean back to about 45 degrees with a long spine and lift the feet off the floor. Hold the dumbbell by its ends in front of the chest.
Breathe out and turn the ribs and shoulders to the right, taking the dumbbell beside the right hip.
Turn through the middle to the left; the knees and feet stay up and still.
Turn back to the right with control.
And to the left again; keep the chest lifted.
Return to the middle, dumbbell in front of the chest, and repeat.

mistakes.mistake: Rounding the back and collapsing the chest
mistakes.fix: Sit tall through the spine; lean back from the hips.
Turn the ribs and shoulders; the dumbbell follows the chest.
Keep the knees together and the feet still in the air.

mistakes.mistake: Going fast with a heavy dumbbell
mistakes.fix: Control each turn and pause; twisting under heavy load is a disc risk.

kinematics.norm: About 45 degrees back from vertical with a long spine (clinical opinion)
Rotation mostly through the thoracic spine, about 40-50 degrees each way (clinical opinion); repeated twisting under load raises disc stress (Marshall 2010)
Feet off the floor, knees bent, held still (clinical opinion)
Held by its ends in front of the chest, travelling beside each hip (clinical opinion)
Controlled, with a pause at each side (clinical opinion)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, a pinching feeling in the front or top of the shoulder, numbness or tingling occurs.
The dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can control for every rep with good form.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Repeated twisting under load stresses the discs; avoid with a disc problem or back pain (McGill 1998; Marshall 2010).
Keep the dumbbell light enough to control every turn.
modify: Back discomfort: put the heels down or drop the dumbbell.
Hip flexor fatigue: rest the heels between sets of turns.
regressions: Bodyweight Russian twist with heels down.
progressions: Slower turns with a 1 s pause.
